item.title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
item.description: History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville's time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment” a mainstream term. These are just a couple of the things we talk about with the legendary musician David Byrne on today's podcast. Byrne's new book, Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up, looks to categorize numerous “sleeping beauties” — ideas that were lost but then rediscovered. Besides Melville and Minsky, we also talk about the lost Roman recipe for concrete and we get into Byrne's thoughts on how to write a song and his own experience of having his music rediscovered by a new generation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Arrested OpenAI Engineer Seeks Bail, Denies Planning to Flee
item.description: The OpenAI software engineer charged with using a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices asked to be freed from custody and denied his purchase of a one-way plane ticket to his native Saudi Arabia was part of a plan to flee US justice.
item.dc:creator: Peter Blumberg

item.title: Wall Street Week | America’s Relationship Woes, Battery Pivot, Farmers’ Fed Warning
item.description: This week, global and business leaders gathered in New Delhi for the Bloomberg New Economy Forum to discuss how the world is redrawing supply chains and investment plans in the face of geopolitical risks. And, in her new book former Canadian deputy prime minister Chrystia Freeland and Former Treasury Secretary Yellen say that the US needs stronger economic ties with its allies. Plus, can storage technologies rescue battery factories built in the hopes of stronger EV adoption? Later, as inflation picks up in the US, the heartland feels the effects more severely. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Pitches AI Safety Bill to Lawmakers
item.description: Anthropic PBC has presented its own draft bill to US lawmakers with a plan for regulating artificial intelligence safety and security, in a moment of heightened concern about the potential risks of the rapidly advancing technology.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary and Samantha Oltman

item.title: JP Morgan Strategist on AI Jitters, Investing Outlook
item.description: Jordan Jackson, JPMorgan Asset Management Global Market Strategist, discusses whether earnings growth may be nearing a peak even if results are not worsening. Jackson agrees that third-quarter results are expected to be strong, with forecasts calling for about 27% to 28% year-over-year earnings growth. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Names Meta Veteran as Litigation Chief in Legal Team Shake-Up
item.description: Apple Inc. has tapped a longtime Meta Platforms Inc. executive as its new litigation chief, bolstering its legal team at a time when the iPhone maker faces a growing array of lawsuits.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: OpenAI Poaches Another SpaceX Sales Lead Focused on AI
item.description: OpenAI has hired SpaceX’s Graham Seamans to lead sales for the firm’s cybersecurity business, the latest in a string of hires from Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence venture.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arroyo

item.title: Thomas Hoenig on Rate Hikes, Inflation Outlook
item.description: Thomas Hoenig said Kevin Warsh’s refusal to signal the Fed’s next move was appropriate and gives policymakers flexibility ahead of the late-October meeting. Hoenig noted that inflation has risen and could climb further, citing energy costs and their spillover into core prices. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Financing The AI Boom: Masters in Business with Bob Michele
item.description: Barry speaks with Bob Michele, CIO and Head of Global Fixed Income, Currency, and Commodities at JPMorgan. They discuss Bob's unconventional start at the University of Pennsylvania, the differences between the science of bonds and the art of equities, and whether the US is heading toward a recession. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint Taps JPMorgan, UBS on Varonis Debt Deal
item.description: Thoma Bravo-backed Proofpoint Inc. has locked in $1.25 billion in financing to support its acquisition of fellow cybersecurity company Varonis Systems Inc., according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Weinman

item.title: Nvidia CEO on AI Market Turmoil: ‘All of This Is Going to Pass’
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang took a sanguine view toward the latest AI stock-market rout, saying the benefits of the technology will soon outweigh the concerns of investors.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Anthropic Signs First Data-Center Deal in Canada With EverWind
item.description: Anthropic PBC signed its first data-center lease in Canada, agreeing to buy capacity at a new project that’s worth more than C$10 billion ($7.1 billion) in the eastern province of Nova Scotia.
item.dc:creator: Nojoud Al Mallees

item.title: Schwab CEO on AI Strategy, Investing Trends, and ‘Charley’
item.description: Rick Wurster, president and CEO at The Charles Schwab Corporation, discusses customer trends in investing, efforts to attract younger investors, and why the firm is blocking unauthorized AI agents. He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Corrects spelling of “Charley” in video headline) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Says iPhone Duo Demand Extraordinary After Delivery Delays
item.description: Apple Inc. said demand for the new iPhone Duo has been “nothing short of extraordinary” after shipping estimates slipped to the end of January of next year just minutes after pre-orders opened on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch and Mark Gurman

item.title: CoreWeave Stock Wipeout Exposes Divide Between AI Fear and Greed
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. has become caught in a tug of war between investors who see rising bond yields as a potential rally killer for the AI trade and those who think demand for computing power will make those concerns seem passe before long.
item.dc:creator: Jeran Wittenstein and Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: EM Stocks, FX Gain on Bets Fed Will Hold Rates This Month
item.description: Gauges of emerging-market currencies and stocks gained on Friday as the greenback extended losses and a selloff in shares related to artificial intelligence abated in Asia.
item.dc:creator: Peter Laca, Marcus Wong and Maria Elena Vizcaino

item.title: Reliance Pushes Back After Musk Questioned Starlink India Delay
item.description: Reliance Industries Ltd., led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, pushed back against suggestions that it is trying to keep Elon Musk’s Starlink Inc. out of India, saying its own satellite venture is still awaiting regulatory clearances.
item.dc:creator: P R Sanjai

item.title: Nvidia Partner GMI Cloud Calls CoreWeave 15% Yield ‘Insane’
item.description: The founder of a cloud computing company with a similar business model to CoreWeave Inc. said the 15% yield on the latter’s bonds is “insane,” compared with the roughly 3.45% rate his company secured on a recent Taiwan dollar loan.
item.dc:creator: Aileen Chuang

item.title: AI Music Deals Are Happening, But How Artists Will Be Paid Remains a Mystery
item.description: How exactly AI money will flow through the music industry remains ambiguous
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: Janus Henderson CEO on Going Private, M&A Deals
item.description: Janus Henderson CEO Ali Dibadj said the firm is energized by its move to private ownership and is using the flexibility to invest in people, technology including AI, new products and client service. He said quarterly earnings pressures had constrained those investments, despite the firm’s growth as a public company. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
